issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and text require a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name, but the implementation (and the example usage in the template main) uses a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether they must implement and store a saloon name (and provide a getter) and which constructor signature to provide.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) implement public SealSaloon(String name) in SealSaloon.java, store the name in a private final String field with a public getter, and update example usage in Main to call new SealSaloon("name"), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to require a parameterless constructor (SealSaloon()) and remove the requirement to store a saloon name. If choosing (A), ensure the constructor still initializes orders (empty Meal[]) and the static stock as required.
